interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 160 and an ISUP grade group 3 pathology from the prostatectomy specimen. Contributing to risk are positive surgical margins and the presence of lymphovascular invasion. Countervailing findings include no documented seminal vesicle invasion and no lymph node metastasis reported in the surgical pathology. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is notable, as the biopsy showed Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) compared to the prostatectomy finding of Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3). Missing postoperative PSA data limits prognostic assessment regarding biochemical recurrence risk. Future prognosis revision would be significantly aided by obtaining a postoperative PSA value and tracking its subsequent trajectory over time. The fixed estimated horizon is 42.09 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 33.67–50.51 months; its coverage has not been validated.
